You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-250 "Cart Maximum Purchase Quantity Enforcement". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- Cart PRD (.docs/prd/cart.md) §2 (CAI-017): "Max 3 units per SKU (same size + colour) per order — error displayed if exceeded." PDP PRD (.docs/prd/pdp.md) §6 (PRD-011): "Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group." These describe the cap two different ways — a flat constant "3" vs. "configurable per customer group" — and may or may not be the same rule (e.g. "3" could just be the currently-configured default for the standard customer group). DO NOT resolve this yourself; surface it as a direct, named clarifying question — this is exactly the kind of ambiguity that should be caught in refinement, not assumed either way during implementation.
- overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts is Tier 1 frozen (owner: Integration/SI Partner) — flag if enforcement needs new logic added there vs. being purely a UI-layer validation against an already-available limit.
- CRM-155 (customer group precedence rules — how overlapping group memberships resolve) is listed as an open/TBD item in the project's live tracker — if PRD-011's "per customer group" framing is confirmed correct, this open item becomes directly relevant (what happens if a customer belongs to two groups with different caps?).

TICKET-SPECIFIC ANGLE: SFCC-271 "Cart Item Component Quantity Stepper" is a separate ticket in this batch that owns the stepper UI. Check whether SFCC-250 (this ticket) owns the actual validation/enforcement logic (with SFCC-271 just consuming a max-limit prop) or whether there's a risk of both tickets independently implementing overlapping enforcement logic.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-250', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20).
2. Fetch SFCC-271 (description only is fine) for the boundary check.
3. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch (cart page, mini-cart, PDP add-to-bag — is enforcement needed at all three entry points, or just cart)? (4) design/Figma dependencies (error-state design)? (5) API/backend dependencies (is the actual cap value sourced from SFCC config, or hardcoded)? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
4. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour (what happens when the customer tries to exceed via the stepper vs. via re-adding from PDP — are both paths covered?), desktop/mobile, a11y (error message announced to screen readers), data (where does the actual numeric limit come from at runtime?) — flag anything genuinely unclear.
5. Design dependency: does a design exist for the error/blocked state?
6. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source
- The CAI-017 vs PRD-011 numeric-conflict flag, stated as a direct clarifying question (name it exactly as above)
- The SFCC-250/SFCC-271 boundary verdict
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

34	## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)

36	- **Guest cart:** persisted for **30 days**

44

47	- 18-month inactivity cleanup
48	- Shareable via email

53	---

55	## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)
56	
57	### Feeds
58	- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
59	- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
60	- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
61	- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

63	### Buffer stock
64	- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
65	- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.

70	- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)

104	
105	*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*
106	
107	- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)

113	## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)
114	
115	- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
116	- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)

118	- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers

122	## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)
123	
124	- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
125	- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
126	- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
127	- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")

132	
133	- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address

140	- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". ## SFCC-250 Backlog Refinement Notes — Research Findings

**Sources checked:** Jira SFCC-250 (full ticket + 1 comment + 1 attachment image), SFCC-271, SFCC-268, SFCC-196 (all issue-linked), JQL searches for a cart-banner ticket; `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/cart.md`, `.docs/prd/pdp.md`, `.docs/prd/account.md`, `.docs/memory/projectState.md`; repo search for `use-current-basket`/`useCurrentBasket` and existing cart component scaffolding.

---

### One-line summary
SFCC-250 wants the cart to show a page-level banner plus a per-line inline message and block further increments once a SKU/size hits its purchase cap — but the ticket is explicitly *not* self-contained: it names two prerequisite components, only one of which has an identifiable Jira story, and the numeric cap itself is owned by a separate, cross-epic PDP config chain.

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **FE impact?** Yes — banner, inline message, and a disabled stepper control are all FE. The cap value and per-SKU basket quantities are read from platform/basket state, not computed in the FE.
2. **Clear enough to size?** Partially. The shopper-facing behaviour has functional sign-off (Emma Kirwan, comment dated 2026-08-31) and a Figma-backed screenshot. But the ticket itself states it "is not a component build story" and names two prerequisite components — only one (Cart Item component) maps to a found ticket (SFCC-271); no ticket was found for the "Page-level banner" component it also names. Not sizeable as-is until that's resolved.
3. **Which surfaces?** SFCC-250's own body text says "banner at the top of the **cart drawer**," and its attached mockup is a drawer-style overlay (top-left "BAG • 3", top-right close X). Its title says "Cart," and the CAI-017 requirement it likely maps to sits under cart.md §2 **"Cart Page"**, not §1 "Mini-Cart" (mini-cart's own PRD section has no max-qty rule at all). So drawer vs. full page vs. both is genuinely unclear — flagged as a question below. PDP's add-to-bag path is **not** in scope here; it's owned by a separate ticket, SFCC-196 "PDP UI – Maximum Purchase Quantity" (Ready for Development).
4. **Design/Figma dependency?** Yes, exists — see Design status below.
5. **API/backend dependency?** Yes. The cap is a Business Manager–configured value, not hardcoded: SFCC-268 "PDP – Maximum Purchase Quantity – BM Config" (global default, status **Ready to deploy to UAT**) is the base config, with SFCC-703 "PDP – Maximum Purchase Quantity Override by Customer Group and SKU" (status **To Do**, blocked by SFCC-196) as the not-yet-built override layer. Both sit under epic SFCC-4 "Product Catalogue," not SFCC-11 "Cart" — SFCC-250 is a downstream consumer of a value owned by a different epic.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture input?** Shared FE/BE, leaning toward needing architecture input: `overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts` (the Tier 1 frozen hook flagged in the brief) **does not exist yet in the repo at all** — confirmed by direct file search. The only current `useCurrentBasket` usages are direct SDK calls in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx` and `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`. No cart page/drawer component folder exists yet under `overrides/app/components` or `overrides/app/pages` either.
7. **Size now or clarify first?** Clarify first — the missing banner-component ticket, the drawer-vs-page surface question, and the numeric-source question (below) all block a confident estimate.

### Four axes

- **Behaviour:** Both overage paths (cart stepper vs. PDP re-add) appear covered, but by two separate tickets using near-identical shopper-story language (SFCC-250 for cart, SFCC-196 for PDP's "clicks Add to Bag multiple times" path) — nothing states they must share a limit-fetch mechanism or be tested together for consistency. **Unclear:** whether a shopper who hits the cap via PDP first, then opens the cart drawer, sees a consistent limit/message from both surfaces.
- **Desktop/mobile:** Only a desktop-width mockup is attached to SFCC-250 (and similarly to SFCC-196). **Unclear:** whether a mobile frame exists at the linked Figma node — not independently verified against Figma itself, only against the Jira-attached screenshot.
- **A11y:** Not addressed in either ticket's description or its one comment. The attached mockup shows the "+" stepper control visually greyed out at max quantity. **Unclear:** whether the banner is meant to be an announced live region (WCAG 2.2 AA per AGENTS.md) and whether the disabled "+" carries an accessible explanation (e.g., `aria-describedby` to the inline message) — none of this is stated as an acceptance criterion.
- **Data:** Global-default cap is BM-configurable and done (SFCC-268); customer-group/SKU override is planned but unstarted (SFCC-703). **Unclear:** where Cart-side (SFCC-250) actually reads the limit and current per-SKU/size basket quantity from at runtime — no stated integration point, and the Tier-1 basket hook that would likely carry this doesn't exist yet.

### Design status + source
**Exists.** Figma: `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann-Designs?node-id=7383-167327` ("Figma is leading" per ticket). Attached screenshot (`image-20260825-052315.png`, Isabel Chaloner, 2026-08-25) shows a desktop cart-drawer with a top banner ("AN ITEM IN YOUR BAG HAS REACHED MAXIMUM QUANTITY") and a per-line inline message ("Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") with the "+" stepper visually disabled. Emma Kirwan gave functional sign-off (2026-08-31) with an explicit caveat: displayed error copy is "purely indicative" and "should be configurable" — not final copy. Desktop-only confirmed; mobile not confirmed from what I could check.

### Numeric-conflict flag — direct clarifying question
Cart PRD §2 (CAI-017) states a flat **"Max 3 units per SKU (same size + colour) per order,"** while PDP PRD §6 (PRD-011) states **"Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group."** Is "3" simply the currently-configured global default within what's actually a fully configurable system, or is there a separate flat cap of 3 that exists independent of the configurable/per-group system? I did not resolve this myself, but found supporting (not conclusive) evidence for the former: SFCC-196's own description states *"SFCC enforces a configurable maximum purchase quantity at a global level. Initially, this will be set at 3,"* and the config chain (SFCC-268 done/UAT-ready → SFCC-703 for per-group/SKU overrides, not started) is built exactly that way. This should still be confirmed explicitly before SFCC-250 is sized, since it determines whether Cart-side enforcement must be customer-group-aware from day one.

### SFCC-250 / SFCC-271 boundary verdict
**Clean on enforcement logic** — no overlap risk. Both tickets explicitly cross-reference each other: SFCC-271 states it "does not cover the enforcement rules that limit or restrict the quantity stepper," naming SFCC-250 for "Maximum SKU quantity enforcement."

**But a narrower real gap exists:** SFCC-250 names "Cart Item component — renders the quantity stepper **and inline warning message**" as one prerequisite. SFCC-271's own scope list (increment/decrement, minimum-quantity state, drawer/summary sync) never mentions building the inline-message UI element itself — it only excludes the *enforcement rules*, not necessarily the static message slot. Someone needs to confirm SFCC-271 also builds that UI slot, or SFCC-250 has to (contradicting its own "not a component build story" framing).

**Separately, a bigger gap:** no ticket was found anywhere in Jira for the "Page-level banner — renders the banner at the top of the cart drawer" component that SFCC-250 also names as a prerequisite (searched the Cart epic and project-wide for "banner"; only match was the unrelated SFCC-51 "Promotional Announcement Banner" under the Navigation epic).

### Specific questions to raise

1. **[PO/BA]** The CAI-017 vs. PRD-011 numeric-conflict question, stated above verbatim.
2. **[BA]** Which ticket builds the "Page-level banner" component SFCC-250 names as a prerequisite? None found in Jira.
3. **[BA]** Does SFCC-271 include building the static inline-warning-message UI slot, or only the stepper logic? SFCC-250 assumes the former; SFCC-271's scope list doesn't say so.
4. **[BA]** Does SFCC-250 cover the cart drawer only, the full cart page only, or both? Its body text says "drawer," its title says "Cart," and CAI-017 sits under the Cart *Page* PRD section, not mini-cart.
5. **[Dev — Integration/SI Partner]** Does Cart-side enforcement read the same BM-configured limit/endpoint the PDP-side stories use, or does it need its own integration point? `overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts` doesn't exist as an override yet — confirm whether this needs new Tier-1 logic or is a pure UI-layer read.
6. **[PO/BA]** If PRD-011's per-customer-group framing is confirmed: CRM-155 (group precedence) is still open/TBD and SFCC-703 (the override story) hasn't started. Can go-live ship on the flat global default alone (SFCC-268, already done) with per-group treated as fast-follow?
7. **[Design]** Confirm a mobile variant of the banner/inline-message/disabled-stepper layout exists at Figma node 7383-167327 — only desktop was attached to the ticket.
8. **[Dev]** A11y: confirm intended screen-reader behaviour for the banner (live-region/alert?) and the disabled "+" control (accessible explanation or bare disabled state?) — not currently stated anywhere in the ticket.

### Readiness call
**Not ready to size** — functional behaviour is signed off and designed, but a likely-unticketed dependency (banner component), an unresolved numeric-source model, and a cross-epic runtime-data dependency all need answers first.
